title: Throughput Slicing and Residency-aware Spillover for Dedicated Shards
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Customers that buy Dedicated capacity need predictable per-customer throughput guarantees across regions while respecting data residency constraints. We currently allow regional pools but lack a first-class mechanism to slice committed throughput into fine-grained dedicated shards and safely spill over traffic when local capacity is exhausted without violating residency policies.

Goal: Implement a coordinated feature called 'Throughput Slicing' (reservation sub-shards) combined with 'Residency-aware Spillover' routing to support: (1) per-shard committed throughput guarantees, (2) controlled short-burst overflow to nearby compliant zones, (3) autoscaling policies that respect residency and warmup constraints, and (4) operational controls to drain/evacuate shards safely.

Scope (this ticket): Design and deliver the control-plane primitives, routing policy, and autoscale policy definitions needed to support throughput slices and residency-aware spillover. Deliverables include: control-plane schema changes, placement policy enum, routing policy implementation, a minimal console UI for configuring slices (separate UX epic will expand), automated tests, and an initial rollout plan for a small group of enterprise customers.
acceptance_criteria: Control-plane accepts 'throughput_slice' reservation objects and surfaces for each dedicated pool: reserved_tokens_per_sec, home_zone, allowed_spillover_zones, max_spill_fraction, burst_window_seconds

Routing policy routes requests to home_zone while local capacity >= reserved_tokens_per_sec, then directs eligible overflow up to max_spill_fraction to allowed_spillover_zones only if those zones are labeled compliant for the customer's residency policy
Autoscaler honors 'min_ready' warmup delay before shifting leftover capacity out of a slice and prevents scale-in within configured safety window (default 5m)
Operator APIs to soft-drain a throughput slice and observe in-console metrics: token throughput, queue depth, spillover-rate, tail latency
Automated unit/integration tests for placement decisions, and an end-to-end canary that verifies residency constraints are never violated under simulated failover
Security review and KMS access checks completed for any cross-zone telemetry and audit logs
tasks: Design control-plane schema additions and migration plan
Implement routing policy changes in request-router service
Extend autoscaler with lease-aware prewarm and scale-in safety windows
Add per-slice telemetry and dashboard panels (console back-end)
Create e2e canary job that simulates zone exhaustion and validates residency policies
Write runbook for soft-drain and emergency-evacuate with rollback steps
decision_log: 2026-02-15: Decided on 'slice-first' model (reserve logical throughput slices inside a regional pool) instead of creating physically isolated per-customer fleets because it reduces cost and preserves packability.
2026-02-20: Chose 'allowed_spillover_zones' whitelist approach for residency compliance to ensure explicit operator control rather than heuristic-based routing.
2026-03-02: Opted for conservative default max_spill_fraction=0.2 and default burst_window_seconds=120s; can be tuned per contract.
2026-03-08: Agreed with security team that cross-zone audit records must include token bucket deltas and a signed residency-decision from the control plane to avoid ambiguous provenance.

implementation_notes: Control-plane: add 'ThroughputSlice' CRD with fields: id, owner_customer_id, reserved_tps, home_zone, allowed_spillover_zones, max_spill_fraction, burst_window_s, min_ready_seconds, immutable_residency_policy_tag

Router: prefer local shard route -> shard_kv_cache check -> if insufficient tokens consult spillover planner -> select target zone with available headroom and residency-allowed flag -> route with transfer token and signed decision
Autoscaler: extend to support 'slice leases' so scale-up can prewarm external zones before moving traffic; implement safety window (configurable) to avoid flapping
Metrics: export per-slice metrics (slice_id.token_consumed, slice_id.queue_depth, slice_id.spillover_count, slice_id.spill_fraction) with labels for zone and residency_tag
Testing: create chaos test that kills home_zone and asserts no request is routed to zones outside allowed_spillover_zones for the duration of the test
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Incorrect whitelist updates could create residency violations. Mitigation: immutable residency tag post-creation and strong validation in control-plane; require two-person approval for changing allowed_spillover_zones for P0 customers.
Risk: Spillover increases cross-zone egress costs and latency. Mitigation: default conservative spill fraction and expose estimated egress cost in console before applying changes.
Risk: Autoscaler prewarm may overshoot and waste capacity. Mitigation: predictive prewarm heuristics with cooldown and anomaly detection on historical short bursts.

Risk: Observability gaps that hide residency breaches. Mitigation: add audit events with signed decisions and automatic alerts for any routing decision that routes outside home_zone when residency is 'strict'
